svg.title: Global cooperation architecture
svg.desc: Proposed European, US and Asia-Pacific cooperation through shared exchange contracts while regional participants retain authority and jurisdictional responsibilities. Proposed global cooperation through open exchange contracts and participant-controlled gateways. European dataspace experience, US innovation and Asia-Pacific initiatives can contribute to shared meaning, discovery and trust under joint governance. Regional participants retain local authority and applicable jurisdictional requirements. Technical interoperability, accepted issuer authority and legal recognition require separate evidence; arrows represent permitted exchanges and governance relationships, not unrestricted data movement or a completed international deployment.

g.text: Europe scales leadership through partnership; participating organizations retain authority over local decisions.

g.text: Meaning | evidence | identity / delegation | policy | requests / receipts | status and version rules

text.style: font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 25px;fill: rgb(27%,38%,47%); stroke:none;

g.text: An agreed interface at each boundary; no mandatory intermediary.

text.style: font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 25px;fill: rgb(27%,38%,47%); stroke:none;

g.text: Arrows denote scoped requests and responses; each receiver checks permission and acceptance.

text.style: font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 25px;fill: rgb(27%,38%,47%); stroke:none;

g.text: Proposed architecture: no automatic mutual recognition, unrestricted data sharing or single global trust root.

text.style: font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 25px;fill: rgb(27%,38%,47%); stroke:none;

g.text: Illustrative equal roles, not one model per region. Operational guarantees require implementation and testing.
